papers.title: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
papers.abstract: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordström and Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. In the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. By searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. The real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. In de Sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. After stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. A prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.

papers.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
papers.abstract: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$β$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$β$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$β$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

papers.title: X-ray Variability of Mrk 421 in 2025 January: A Ten-Day XPoSat XSPECT Campaign with Contemporaneous NICER Coverage
papers.abstract: We present an X-ray study of the high-synchrotron-peaked blazar Mrk 421 using ten days of XPoSat/XSPECT observations (2025 January 20-29; 202 ks) and contemporaneous NICER data. The 0.8-15 keV light curve has a fractional variability amplitude of 19.6 +/- 0.3 per cent, and Bayesian blocks resolve 26 flux states spanning a factor of 2.3. The best-constrained flare has a fast rise and a slow decay, with e-folding times of about 3 h and 30 h. For typical jet parameters, the X-ray-emitting electrons cool faster than this, suggesting that the decay traces a gradual weakening of their acceleration. The count-rate distribution is best described by two lognormal components, consistent with multiplicative variability. The power spectrum is a red-noise power law with a slope of about 1.7 over timescales of 25 min to 10 d, typical of blazars. XSPECT and NICER count rates are well correlated over eight matched epochs (r = 0.941). We fitted log-parabola models to day-resolved spectra from XSPECT, NICER and both jointly, and to flux-resolved XSPECT spectra. Both show spectral hardening with brightness. In the flux-resolved spectra, the photon index at 1 keV decreases from 2.24 in the faintest state to 1.96 in the brightest, and the synchrotron peak moves from about 0.66 to 1.06 keV, while the curvature ($β\approx 0.7$) shows no significant change. Power-law fits to Bayesian blocks show that bright blocks at the same rate can differ in photon index by up to $6.4σ$, so count rate alone does not fix the spectral state.

papers.title: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey
papers.abstract: We report the detection of two single dispersed pulses with widths of about 6.7\,ms and 15.6\,ms and flux densities of about 0.8 and 1.7\,Jy. These were found in a blind survey of two circular regions (Dec$\;=+22^{\circ}$ and $+5^{\circ}$,RA: 0--24~h) at high radio frequencies \mbox{(4400--5000\,MHz)} using four 4-channel filter radiometers (central frequencies of 4475, 4625, 4775, and 4925\,MHz) spanning a total frequency bandwidth of 600\,MHz. The survey was carried out with the Western Sector antenna of the RATAN-600 radio telescope, which had an effective area of 1200\,m$^2$ in~2017--2025. The total area of the survey was about 1500~square degrees, and each pointing of the antenna lasted one year. We consider these to be two rare, high-frequency FRB events (MJD~58614.38257 and MJD~58659.62482), detected with estimated dispersion measures of $200\pm20$ and $266\pm10$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ at a final signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level of 8--9 after additional optimal filtration. After subtraction of the estimated dispersions within the Milky Way, we estimated redshifts of approximately 0.09 and 0.13, respectively, using the traditional equation: ${\rm DM}\,[{\rm pc~cm}^{-3}] = 1000\,z$ for the intergalactic medium. The estimated isotropic energies of the FRBs are equal to $10^{40}$\,erg and $2\times 10^{40}$\,erg, respectively. To effectively detect single pulses, we applied machine learning methods using a neural network trained on synthetic FRB pulse profiles.

papers.title: Hidden by Exponential Screening: The Invisibility of the Dymnikova Black Hole de Sitter Core to Accretion Observables
papers.abstract: The Dymnikova spacetime replaces the Schwarzschild singularity with a de Sitter core, and its lapse deviates from Schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2M)}$. Whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. We address it with GRHD simulations of BHL accretion onto Dymnikova BH for six values of the critical length, $0.1M\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1M$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. All runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. The dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7M$. Because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. The time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2σ)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3M)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0M$ and $31.6\pm0.4M)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. Accretion onto a Dymnikova BH is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. More broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

papers.title: Mass and angular momentum assessement of the neutron star XTEJ 1807-294 using X-ray triplets
papers.abstract: The X-ray power-density spectrum of the accreting millisecond pulsar XTEJ 1807-294 contains several triplets of simultaneously observed quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs): a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. This fact allows us to assess the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star. We also apply an error propagation formula to obtain interval estimates of the parameters of the star. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs. The degree of consistency of the bounds obtained with the different triplets may provide information for the viability of the used models.

papers.title: Cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory: Analytic treatment
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory. The onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged Reissner-Nordström black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. In the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs theory. In particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{μ_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $μ\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the Yang-Mills field due to the Higgs effect). Interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${μ_{k+1}/{μ_{k}}}=e^{-{{2π}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.

papers.title: Self-lensing of electromagnetic counterparts to extreme mass ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on inclined orbits can produce recurrent electromagnetic flares by shocking gas at accretion-disk crossings. Using forward ray tracing in Kerr spacetime, we investigate how self-lensing by the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) reshapes these flares. Flares emitted behind the SMBH can be strongly magnified, whereas near-side flares remain almost unmagnified, producing strong-weak alternation even for identical intrinsic emission. As Lense-Thirring precession shifts the crossing azimuths, it generates long-term amplitude envelopes whose spacing can be used to infer the precession period. Lense-Thirring precession can also increase the cumulative geometric lensing probability over longer observing windows. Within individual flares, Keplerian motion of hotspots co-rotating with the disk produces time-dependent magnification, which can generate shoulders or double peaks and change the effective width. We also propose a spectral diagnostic to distinguish self-lensing from external lensing when their light curves are similar: self-lensing can amplify later, cooler emission and produce a softer secondary peak, whereas delayed images from a static external lens repeat the same intrinsic spectral evolution.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Signal from a Short GRB Relativistic MHD Jet
papers.abstract: We analyze the gravitational-wave (GW) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of a short GRB jet with parameters corresponding to those of GRB 170817A. The signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the GRBs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized Einstein equations of an MHD simulation. Separating the GW signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. The waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$Hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the GRB duration. A pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the GW signal can reveal processes deep in the GRB engine that cannot be observed otherwise. The signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. The total radiated GW energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal E}^2/τ$ with the shortest variability time $τ$, so this is a lower limit. Comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to GW170817 are marginally detectable by DECIGO from up to 10 Mpc and by the Einstein Telescope from 1 Mpc. The injected Poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. An engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some GRB models, would substantially increase the GW energy and detectability.

papers.title: Signatures of quark matter from neutron star mass-radius curve
papers.abstract: Signatures of the presence of quark matter inside neutron stars are obtained from the analysis of more than 250,000 mass-radius curves that describe nucleonic, hyperonic and hybrid stars, based on five different hadronic relativistic mean-field models and four different descriptions of quark matter. A radius maximum occurring above $1.7\,M_\odot$ strongly favors quark matter inside the star. A second criterion identifying the presence of quark matter is $X>-0.2$km, where X=[R(2.0)-R(1.6)]-[R(1.6)-R(1.4)] is obtained from the radius of stars with 2.0, 1.6 and 1.4 $M_\odot$. It is also shown that most of the hyperonic stars have a radius maximum that peaks around 1.5$M_\odot$ and compactness below 0.27 for the maximum-mass configuration, while for the nucleonic stars that have a radius maximum, this peaks below 1.3$M_\odot$ and the compactness of the maximum-mass configuration lies above 0.26.

papers.title: A magnetically heated slim disc-corona model for tidal disruption events
papers.abstract: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) can reach super-Eddington luminosities near their peak. While their optical/UV emission may arise from multiple processes, X-rays are more likely to be produced by the innermost accretion flow close to the black hole, analogous to super-Eddington flows in stellar-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) and active galactic nuclei (AGNs). Super-Eddington AGNs typically show disc-dominated spectra, with weak and steep coronae, while super-Eddington XRBs show a wider variety of spectral shapes. Here we explore disc-corona coupling in TDEs by developing a super-Eddington ($\dot{m}>1$: slim) disc model in which magnetic reconnection transfers some of the accretion power from the disc into a hot Comptonizing corona. We test the model on the well-monitored X-ray TDE AT2021ehb, and can broadly fit the brightest X-ray spectra with a black-hole mass $M_{\rm BH}\sim10^6$--$10^7\,M_\odot$ at $\dot m\sim 1$, but need variable magnetic coupling to the disc to match the large observed fast changes in coronal contribution. AGN at similarly high luminosity do not show such variable coronae, but the transient XRB outbursts do, suggesting that it may be a common feature of rapidly changing, non-steady accretion flows. As the TDE declines to $\dot{m}\sim 0.01$, the source hardens, but never goes below $Γ\sim 2$, unlike both AGN and XRB at these luminosities. Thus the X-ray spectral evolution in this TDE does not resemble either XRB or AGN in detail, likely pointing to the very different, highly variable nature of the accretion flow in a tidal disruption event.

papers.title: Chemical abundances of a Galactic Centre ejecta discovered in DESI
papers.abstract: Chemical abundances in the Galactic Centre (GC) are challenging to measure because of high extinction, crowding, and distance, and are typically limited to the brightest AGB and M giants observed in the near-infrared. In contrast, hypervelocity stars (HVSs) ejected from the GC by Sgr A* carry their natal composition into accessible regions such as the Milky Way halo, making them unique probes of GC chemistry. We present high-resolution optical Magellan/MIKE spectroscopy of DESI-312, a bound HVS candidate in the halo with super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{Fe/H}]=0.2\pm0.1$). This sets it apart from accreted halo populations on radial orbits and is most naturally explained by GC formation and Hills-mechanism ejection. Updated isochrone fits give an age of 7.4-11.3 Gyr; together with its metallicity and kinematics, this strengthens the case for a GC origin. Korg and Turbospectrum spectral synthesis yields $[\mathrm{X/Fe}]$ for 22 elements, plus Li from an independent line-by-line NLTE analysis. As DESI-312 is near the main sequence, its C, N, and O abundances are unaltered by dredge-up; to our knowledge, these are the first such measurements of unevolved GC material. Its abundance pattern lies where the nuclear star cluster (NSC), nuclear stellar disc (NSD), and inner-bulge sequences overlap, with a Na enhancement ($[\mathrm{Na/Fe}]=+0.16^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$) more modest than in NSC giants of similar metallicity. Chemistry alone thus cannot identify its progenitor; we nevertheless favour the NSC, given its large reservoir of old, metal-rich stars and the star's kinematics. Alongside WINERED-HVS1 and the S-star S0-6/S10, whose abundances point to different progenitors, this tentatively suggests multiple progenitor populations for the S-star cluster. DESI-312 is a test case for sampling GC chemistry with ejected dwarfs at optical wavelengths, complementing near-infrared studies of giants.

papers.title: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10
papers.abstract: We present the timing solution of the millisecond pulsar PSR J1657-0406A in the globular cluster M10, based on observations performed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The timing results show that PSR J1657-0406A is in a long-period ($P_b \sim 37$ days) and eccentric ($e \sim 0.12$) orbit. We also measured the periastron advance $\dotω = 0.00090(13)$ degrees per year, which implies a total system mass of $2.5(6)$ solar masses, assuming that general relativity accurately models the orbital motion. No optical counterpart was detected within the positional uncertainty, indicating that the companion is unlikely to be a main-sequence star. Considering possible formation channels for the orbital eccentricity, we favor a helium white dwarf companion, although a massive white dwarf or neutron star cannot be completely excluded.

papers.title: Angle-dependent emission from evolving accretion layers
papers.abstract: Photon propagation through an evolving atmosphere can change the angular distribution of emerging radiation even when its integrated optical column remains constant. We quantify this effect in an irradiated, internally heated, expanding plane-parallel layer using grey, special-relativistic similarity solutions. The full angular radiation field determines both the source function and the acceleration of a pressureless flow in prompt radiative balance. We compare each evolving solution with two frozen transport calculations on the same density and velocity profiles, holding the source fixed in one and allowing it to relax in the other. Heating produces the familiar transition from limb darkening to limb brightening, while the temporal correction to the angular contrast changes sign with optical column. For an upper boundary moving at $0.04c$, an injection speed of $0.06c$, and heating four times the reference incident flux, the intensity ratio between direction cosines $0.1$ and $1$ exceeds the frozen, fixed-source result by $18.8$ per cent at column $τ_0=0.15$, but is smaller by $2.53$ per cent at $τ_0=0.55$. Source relaxation preserves this reversal. The corresponding direct photon flight times are one third and three per cent of the flow age in the oblique and normal directions, respectively. These solutions provide a controlled local benchmark for temporal angular transfer in evolving disc atmospheres and reprocessing layers; application to a specific accreting system requires thermal, spectral, and geometrical physics beyond the present model.

papers.title: Magnetized Accretion Flows with Low Angular Momentum Around Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the global structure of slowly rotating accretion flows around black holes in the presence of large-scale magnetic fields. Using a steady, height-integrated transonic model with radial mass loss, we examine how magnetic pressure, tension, and torque modify the dynamics of Bondi-like and disk-like accretion. Adopting a radial magnetic-field prescription based on results from previous numerical simulations, we compare hydrodynamical and magnetized solutions across a range of plasma-$\rm β$ values, from weak to strong field regimes. We find that magnetic stresses substantially alter the sonic radius and change the angular momentum and mass accretion rate reaching the black hole. For sufficiently strong fields, the inner flow becomes highly sub-Keplerian and magnetically dominated ($ β= P_{\mathrm{gas}}/ P_{\mathrm{mag}}<1$), and magnetic stresses can drive transitions to lower angular momentum. We also show that outflows in this magnetized accretion flow can significantly alter the structure of disk-like accretion. We further perform 2D simulations of magnetized Bondi accretion and torus accretion and find that the radial structure and magnetically dominated, sub-Keplerian character of our semi-analytical solutions are qualitatively reproduced.

papers.title: The Birth of Plasmoids: Weibel-Driven Secondary Tearing and its Suppression in Relativistic Reconnection
papers.abstract: Plasmoids, or magnetic islands, dominate relativistic reconnection layers in kinetic simulations, yet the instability that creates them remains poorly understood. By tracking newborn islands in 2D particle-in-cell simulations of pair-plasma reconnection with magnetizations $0.1\leσ_0\le1000$, we show that plasmoids are seeded by a current-filamentation/Weibel instability driven by counter-streaming out-of-plane current carriers near primary x-lines. Measured growth rates are $\sim0.1$ times the background plasma frequency and agree with linear theory evaluated on the simulated distributions. As inflowing plasma loads the sheet away from the x-line, the current is carried by more particles and their out-of-plane drift slows. The filamentation instability shuts off once this drift becomes comparable to the momentum spread in the outflow direction, which occurs at a distance $\ell_{\rm iso}\proptoσ_0$ from the x-line. Because the unstable region extends farther at higher $σ_0$, our results account for the onset of plasmoid-dominated reconnection in the relativistic regime but predict that plasmoid formation is suppressed beyond $\sim\ell_{\rm iso}$ from primary x-lines, even in ultra-relativistic reconnection. Particle acceleration, variability, and coherent radio emission attributed to plasmoid-dominated reconnection may therefore be confined to smaller regions than previously assumed.

papers.title: Effects of Competing Reactions on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ on Abundance Distributions in Type I X-Ray Bursts
papers.abstract: The composition of X-ray burst ashes affects the thermal transport properties of the neutron star crust, as well as heating and cooling through weak interaction processes. Reaction-rate uncertainties can produce secondary peaks separated from the main peak in final abundance distributions. Using STARLIB reaction rates and their temperature-dependent uncertainties in the K04 one-zone post-processing model, we combine four sets of Monte Carlo calculations with XGBoost classification, SHAP analysis, and reaction-flow analysis to investigate the origins of these secondary peaks. We find that the competing $(p,α)$ and $(p,γ)$ reaction pairs on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ are primarily responsible for secondary peaks outside the central 68\% confidence interval in all 44 isotopes examined. Fixing both pairs at their median rates reduces the fractions of samples in the secondary-peak regions by 96\%--100\%, while the bounds of the central 68\% interval remain largely unchanged for most mass numbers. The $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ pair has the larger effect. Enhanced recycling limits the supply of material to heavier isotopes and accelerates proton consumption, while earlier proton exhaustion further suppresses subsequent proton captures. These changes alter the balance between isotope production and destruction, leading to high- or low-abundance secondary peaks over a broad mass range beyond the Ni--Cu and Zn--Ga cycles. These results identify $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}(p,γ)^{60}\mathrm{Zn}$ and the two competing channels on $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ as priorities for further nuclear-physics constraints to improve XRB abundance predictions.

papers.title: Detecting Muons with a Siemens Biograph Vision Quadra
papers.abstract: Atmospheric muons are routinely detected with a variety of instruments, from cloud chambers to scintillation detectors. In this study, we demonstrate that atmospheric muons can also be detected with a clinical long axial field-of-view positron emission tomograph (PET). We performed a blank scan without any radioactive source, using a prototype feature that records all single crystal interactions. The energy a muon deposits in the PET crystals far exceeds the upper limit of the recorded energy range, which means muons cannot be identified through energy discrimination. Instead, we used the scanner's time-of-flight capabilities to select crossing events, i.e. pairs of high-energy single crystal events across the PET gantry whose spatial and temporal separation is consistent with a downward-going ultrarelativistic particle. Random pairings, however, cannot be rejected on an event-by-event basis. We therefore established the muon origin of the crossing events through their characteristic angular distribution. In order to account for geometry and event selection bias, we compare the measured crossing events to a Monte Carlo simulation of muons following the expected angular distribution. This confirms that the measured crossing events in the PET scanner are consistent with atmospheric muons.

papers.title: Angular Momentum Transport across Accretion States around a rapidly spinning black hole
papers.abstract: Accretion requires the outward transport of angular momentum, but the relative contributions of matter advection, turbulent stresses, ordered magnetic fields, winds, and black-hole spin remain uncertain in strongly magnetized flows. We use high-resolution three-dimensional GRMHD simulations around a rapidly rotating black hole ($a=0.998$) to compare SANE, intermediate-flux, and magnetically arrested disk states. In SANE and intermediate states, outward stresses are insufficient to overcome inward angular-momentum advection, and the net flux remains inward. In MAD, ordered Maxwell stresses regulate the disk and drive winds, while the Blandford-Znajek jet carries a distinct, near-constant flux extracted from the black hole, making the total angular-momentum flux outward. Magnetic-flux eruptions modulate both channels. During an eruption, an equatorial current sheet extends beyond the ergosphere, and low-density, magnetically dominated bubbles of expelled flux enter the polar region. The jet becomes asymmetric, its tilt more than doubles, and its opening angle first widens and then contracts below its pre-eruption value. Eruptions suppress the horizon accretion rate and briefly reverse the angular-momentum flux through the jet surface, while reorganizing the Maxwell stresses in the disk. As horizon-threading flux re-accumulates, the turbulent stress recovers toward its saturated MAD level. Eruption durations and lags among horizon flux, accretion rate, and jet tilt of ~40-90 $r_g/c$ correspond to milliseconds for stellar-mass black holes and tens of minutes for Sgr A*. These results distinguish disk-regulating magnetic torques from black-hole-sourced jet transport and show how flux eruptions couple disk accretion, winds, and jet morphology.

papers.title: Deconvolved IXPE Polarization Maps of the Crab Nebula in a Maximum-a-Posteriori Framework
papers.abstract: We analyze the first IXPE observation of the Crab Nebula using a polarization-resolved deconvolution method based on maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. The method reconstructs the polarization-resolved intensity map as a three-dimensional distribution in sky-position and polarization-angle spaces, using an instrumental response that depends on the incident direction and polarization angle of X-ray photons. We apply the method to the IXPE data in the 2-8~keV band and compare the result with that obtained using the basic analysis. Our result shows sharper spatial structure, making the jet shape more clearly identifiable than that in the basic analysis. The reconstructed image shows a statistically significant tendency for the magnetic-field orientation to be perpendicular to the intensity-gradient orientation in the jet region. Although these results are obtained by using a simplified response where systematic uncertainty remains, they demonstrate that our MAP-based deconvolution can improve the interpretability of IXPE polarization maps for nebular sources.

papers.title: Extreme Hard X-ray Variability in the TeV Blazar Mrk 421: Insights from NuSTAR Observations
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the hard X-ray variability of the TeV blazar Mrk 421 over both long-term and intra-day timescales to gain insights into the particle acceleration and cooling mechanisms driving its emission. Using 27 NuSTAR observations spanning 2012 to 2024, we conduct detailed spectral and timing analyses. Our findings reveal pronounced flux variability, with changes by up to a factor of 200 over the decade and a 10-fold increase within a period of 15 days during a flaring episode. The flux distribution exhibits a lognormal profile, and a linear root-mean-square (RMS)--flux relation suggests a multiplicative variability process. Spectral analysis indicates that a log-parabolic model best describes most observations, with a strong linear anti-correlation between the photon index and curvature parameter. We also identify a positive correlation between the synchrotron peak energy and flux, accompanied by a subtle ``harder-when-brighter'' trend. These results align with standard blazar emission models, supporting particle acceleration via shock fronts or magnetic reconnection in the relativistic jet.

papers.title: Symmetry energy effect on hot nuclear matter and proto-neutron stars
papers.abstract: We examine the effects of symmetry energy on proto-neutron stars (PNSs) by employing equation of state (EOS) described by the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model. The thermal properties of dense matter and the bulk properties of PNSs are investigated under the assumptions of isothermy, isentropy, and fixed lepton fractions. The polytropic index is calculated at finite temperature, revealing a negative correlation with the PNS maximum mass that the EOS can support. The properties of PNSs during the heating and cooling stages along their evolution line are explored under different combinations of lepton fraction and entropy. We investigate the correlation between the symmetry energy slope $L$ and the properties of PNSs. As $L$ increases, the PNS radius also increases; however, this effect diminishes with a growing lepton fraction for the isentropic case. These results indicate that the nuclear symmetry energy and its density dependence play crucial roles in determining the properties of PNSs and their evolution stages.

papers.title: Higher-Order Symmetry Energy Effects on the Properties of Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: We study the effects of the symmetry-energy curvature $K_{\rm sym}$ on the equation of state (EoS) and neutron-star properties within the relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework. We construct controlled families of RMF parametrizations based on the TM1 and IUFSU models by varying $K_{\rm sym}$ while keeping the symmetry energy $J$ and its slope $L$ fixed at saturation density. We find that, although a larger $K_{\rm sym}$ leads to a lower symmetry energy at suprasaturation densities and a reduced proton fraction in $β$-equilibrated matter, it results in a stiffer EoS and a higher sound speed. The maximum neutron-star mass is weakly affected, whereas the canonical radius $R_{1.4}$ exhibits a nearly linear dependence on $K_{\rm sym}$.

papers.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
papers.abstract: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. To produce the radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed to be most likely an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of $-(6.8-9.6)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$ when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD ($1.4~M_\odot$). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than $1.4~M_\odot$ if the measured period derivative exceeds $-9.6\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra-contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a $1.0-1.6~M_\odot$ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of $-(4.9-13.5)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of $1.35-1.5~M_\odot$. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be $0.006$ when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

papers.title: The light curve modeling of eclipsing cataclysmic variables: from period bouncers to nova-likes
papers.abstract: I describe the basic concepts used in developing the computer code CVlab V2.0, which simulates the light curves of close binary systems with accretion-disk structures. I provide a detailed description of the code, including its underlying assumptions, limitations, and applications, as well as prospects for future development.

papers.title: Exothermic Higgs portal: from LUX-ZEPLIN recoil to Gamma Rays
papers.abstract: We show that a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM) by a single complex scalar $φ$ provides a viable inelastic exothermic, thermal relic, interpretation of the recently reported nuclear-recoil candidate from LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). The mass terms and Higgs-portal interactions split $φ$ into two nearly degenerate real scalars, $φ_{1,2}$. For mass-splitting of a few hundred keV, $φ_2$ is cosmologically long-lived and the two states have comparable relic abundances. Taking $φ_{1,2}$ masses to be $\sim100\,$GeV, with off-diagonal Higgs coupling fixed by relic abundance, the exothermic down-scattering yields an order-one event expectation for the LZ exposure, without relying on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter velocity distribution required in endothermic scenarios. This scenario can be tested using different nuclear targets and with indirect dark matter searches: $φ_2\toφ_1γγ$ decays give a broad sub-MeV photon continuum that can be probed by INTEGRAL/SPI and COSI; $φ_1φ_2$ annihilation produces a GeV-scale continuum, extending up to $\sim$100 GeV, that is probed by Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf galaxies; current CMB constraints are satisfied and annihilation among dark matter particles captured in the Sun is strongly suppressed. Next-generation experiments could probe correlated scattering, decay, and annihilation signatures of this thermal Higgs-portal scenario.

papers.title: Probing the nature of Galactic microquasars with diffuse gamma rays and neutrinos: low-mass versus high-mass X-ray binaries
papers.abstract: The observations of sub-PeV gamma-ray emission have provided strong evidence for a Galactic origin of the cosmic-ray "knee" region. Meanwhile, mounting observations have ruled out most supernova remnants as sources of PeV cosmic rays, i.e., the so-called PeVatrons. Recently, a new type of PeVatron candidate, microquasars, has received much attention. Studies indicate that microquasars could be the dominant contributor to PeV cosmic rays. However, the spatial distribution of microquasars is not known. They could belong to either LMXBs or HMXBs, depending on the mass of the optical companion star. In this work, we study which type could be the dominant by means of very high energy gamma rays and neutrinos. We find that the diffuse gamma-ray distributions along the Galactic longitude are quite different due to the spatial distributions of these two kinds of sources. If the very high energy gamma rays are dominated by the distribution of LMXBs, the gamma-ray distribution would be more concentrated toward the direction of the Galactic center. Furthermore, we also find that HMXB distribution cannot account for the latest observations of Galactic diffuse neutrinos. Higher-precision measurements of the Galactic diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino fluxes with LHAASO, HAWC, IceCube, and KM3NeT will allow the spatial distribution of the microquasar population to be determined and the origin of the knee to be tested.

papers.title: From Kination to Detection: Scotogenic Scalar Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar dark matter in the scotogenic model during an early kination-dominated epoch. The enhanced expansion rate causes earlier freeze-out and increases the relic abundance, opening viable dark matter masses from approximately $200~\mathrm{GeV}$ to $1~\mathrm{TeV}$ while reducing the need for co-annihilation with a nearly degenerate singlet fermion. Current indirect searches strongly constrain the $(100-200)~\mathrm{GeV}$ region, whereas much of the surviving parameter space can be probed by CTA and next-generation direct detection experiments. The viable spectra also lead to complementary collider signatures, including missing transverse energy, displaced leptons, and disappearing charged tracks, providing promising tests at the HL-LHC and future lepton colliders.

papers.title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
papers.abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. Using public atmospheric reanalysis data and records of cosmic-ray, solar, and geomagnetic variability, we reproduce the measured seasonal response of the IceCube muon rate. We then test whether the same response applies to long-term temperature changes with a different vertical temperature profile. The limiting requirement is detector stability rather than counting statistics: an unmodeled muon rate drift of $1\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$ would mimic a temperature trend of $2.8\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. The long-term rate must therefore be stable to approximately $0.3\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$. Within this budget, snow accumulation contributions can be constrained. For a 14-year record, atmospheric variability gives a one-sided 95% CL statistical sensitivity of $1.6\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. Given this sensitivity, the $\sim0.9\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$ cooling indicated by the 2011-2025 atmospheric records would become distinguishable after approximately 30 years of measurement.

papers.title: A Unified Mass-Loading Model for ASKAP J1745-5051: Linking Long-Period Radio Transients to Magnetic Cataclysmic Variables
papers.abstract: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) in white dwarf binaries require sufficiently tenuous plasma to sustain coherent radio emission, posing a challenge in systems with dense accretion flows. ASKAP J1745-5051 (J1745) combines LPT-like radio pulses recurring approximately every 82 min with magnetic accretion and X-ray modulation at a consistent period. We investigate this coexistence using a unified mass-loading framework for Roche-lobe overflow and a tenuous donor wind in the binary magnetic field. The dense stream supplies the accretion curtain and near-white-dwarf X-ray sources, while the tenuous wind feeds flux tubes of $(1-4)\times10^7\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$, satisfying the local density requirement for electron-cyclotron maser emission. A fiducial geometry places the X-ray maximum near orbital phase $0.886$ and produces a radio-visibility window at phases $0.22-0.33$, consistent with the primary observed pulse window. Geometrical modulation and curtain absorption produce stronger soft-band than hard-band X-ray variability. Long-term phase-connected radio monitoring and simultaneous X-ray observations can test this interpretation through recurring radio phase changes and correlated changes in X-ray modulation. These results extend the proposed connection between detached binary LPTs and magnetic cataclysmic variables (mCVs). J1745 may represent an evolved mCV near the orbital-period minimum, suggesting that LPT-like activity can occur at a late accreting stage.

papers.title: A temporally clustered gravitational wave pair and a Type IIb supernova
papers.abstract: Compact object mergers are generally expected long after the stellar collapse that forms their remnants. Here we report two marginal gravitational wave (GW) candidates, S190910d and S190910h, separated by 7.1 hr, whose three-dimensional localizations overlap at the position and distance of the Type IIb supernova SN 2019rsq. The GW pair lies in the extreme tail of the joint distribution of temporal separation and localization overlap, with a pairwise null probability of $7.6 \times 10^{-5}$ under our Monte Carlo null test. Independent re-analyses recover both as signal-like candidates. Under a common-origin hypothesis, S190910h remains consistent with a low-mass compact binary with source-frame masses near $2.5 + 1.3\,M_\odot$, whereas S190910d favours a strongly asymmetric $\sim 34 + 3\,M_\odot$ system whose observed amplitude is compatible with the supernova distance. SN 2019rsq is a rapidly evolving stripped-envelope Type IIb explosion whose light curve is consistent with stellar collapse occurring near the GW activity. Although the supernova coincidence alone is not statistically rare, its timing and physical properties provide a stellar collapse anchor for the unusual GW pair. A fragmenting collapsar disk provides a plausible framework that can accommodate the component masses, hour-scale delays and supernova properties, raising the possibility that multiple compact object mergers can accompany a single stellar collapse episode.

papers.title: CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS): Power Spectrum Injections and Survey Sensitivity
papers.abstract: Artificial signal injection into real data is a key tool in time-domain radio astronomy, with particular import to the study of pulsars and Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs). Many surveys inject into the time series to probe observational biases impacting the detection of radio transients. In the case of the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stack Search (CHAMPSS), the computational demands of both hardware and software time series injections force an alternative approach. We present methods for injecting artificial pulsar signals into the Fourier power spectrum. The injection process detailed here is computationally negligible compared to the overhead of the CHAMPSS search pipeline. We use injections to probe the in-system biases of the CHAMPSS survey. CHAMPSS is most sensitive to pulsars with frequencies on the order of 0.1 - 100 Hz and fluxes > 1 mJy. Our injections show weak overall sensitivity dependence on other factors such as dispersion measure (DM), duty cycle, and sky coordinates, but complex non-monotonic interactions between all parameters. Our findings suggest that frequency-dependent noise, especially low-frequency or "red" noise, and sampling limitations at higher frequencies are the dominant extrinsic factors decreasing CHAMPSS' sensitivity to pulsars.

papers.title: The Valence and Inner Shell Ionization Properties of Sr I - III by Non-Thermal Electrons in Kilonovae
papers.abstract: The presence of strontium (Z = 38) was identified from spectra of the first multi-messenger kilonova transient, AT2017gfo, with the evolution of its spectral signature indicating a rapidly changing ionization balance. Interpretation of spectra at later times requires a more detailed understanding of recombination and ionization processes, including ionization by `non-thermal' electrons produced by beta decay. Published measurements of the ionization cross sections of Sr I and Sr II show complex structures likely arising from excitation autoionization. Using the Flexible Atomic Code we report calculations of the valence and inner shell ionization cross sections for Sr I, Sr II, and Sr III, and recover similar structures in the ionization cross sections. Though no measurements exist for Sr III, the calculations suggest negligible contributions from excitation autoionization. These new data are incorporated into Spencer-Fano models of non-thermal electron degradation and coupled to an ionization balance solver. The effects of excitation autoionization, treated as excitation with the additional production of an Auger electron, on the degradation spectra of non-thermal are explored. Calculations at both level- and configuration-average resolution return ion fractions that agree within 5-20%. The calculations probe the impact of including final-charge-state-resolved branching ratios for inner shell ionization which result in multi-ionization events from successive Auger cascades. Omission of these branching ratios is shown to have large impacts on the ionization balance. The calculated cross sections will be provided on Zenodo.

papers.title: Slowly rotating white dwarfs in f (R, T ) = R + 2λT gravity: structure and stationary tidal response
papers.abstract: We calculate the structure and stationary tidal response of cold carbon fluid white dwarfs in $f(R,T)=R+2λT$ gravity through second order in uniform rotation. Equilibria are compared at fixed baryon number, with angular momentum also conserved during each aligned electric quadrupolar tidal perturbation. Negative coupling increases radii and dimensional tidal deformabilities over the common mass range. For the baryon sequence studied, background readjustment accounts for 95.8--97.5\% of the rotational enhancement at 40\% of each model's Kepler reference frequency. The explicit mixed rotational tidal contribution is positive and numerically resolved, but subdominant. At that spin, the enhancement relative to each coupling's static model decreases from 107.4\% in general relativity to 14.2\% at the most negative coupling, despite its larger absolute deformability. This reduction reflects less relative background expansion and a different Love-number variation.

papers.title: Proposal for the resolution of the disagreement between DAMA and other Underground Dark Matter Experiments
papers.abstract: It is a great mystery still needing a solution that the underground experiments looking for dark matter disagree, in tIt is a great mystery still needing a solution that the underground experiments looking for dark matter disagree, in the sense that DAMA/LIBRA has found dark matter with a confidence level of several standard deviations, while neither the xenon based experiments nor even the experiments using the same target material NaI(Tl) as DAMA see the same amount of dark matter. We propose to solve this enigma by postulating that the dark matter gets excited during its passage through the mountain shielding from outer space down to the experimental halls; the DAMA experiment is namely about twice as deep as the ANAIS and COSINE-100 experiments, so that there is longer passage time for DAMA, which thus gets more excited dark matter particles. The xenon-scintillator experiments have their strong limits for dark matter making itself felt via nucleus recoils, and thus we can just assume that the excited dark matter mainly emits e.g. electrons, and the xenon-experiments would hardly see such dark matter. The single event recently seen by LUX/ZEPPELIN could be due to a low rate of nucleus emission in addition to the hypothesised electrons.

papers.title: Probing the geometry and outflows of the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 with multi-band polarimetry
papers.abstract: We present VLT/FORS2 R- and I-band imaging polarimetry of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar SAXJ1808.4-3658 during its 2025 outburst, coordinated with the first X-ray polarimetric observations of this source with IXPE. We detect significant optical linear polarisation at every epoch (polarisation degree P~0.3-1.5%, angle Phi ~ 8-48°), consistent with the only prior optical polarimetric campaign of this source, obtained during a previous outburst. The average optical polarisation angle is offset by ~16-24° from the IXPE angle of the persistent X-ray emission, which pulse-profile modelling shows to trace the spin axis. A fast-timing sequence reveals the optical polarisation angle swinging by up to ~40° within minutes, disfavouring scattering in the disc. A colour-magnitude diagram and the dependence of the optical polarisation on the red colour excess over the disc emission, which we attribute to the jet, instead point to a jet origin during the main outburst, consistent with contemporaneous radio detections. The offset, with the same mean optical angle as in the previous outburst, can arise from emission near a wide jet base, where the Doppler-boosted side of the cone dominates. At the onset of the reflaring stage the optical polarisation degree is highest and its angle coincides with the IXPE one, while the disc likely dominates the optical flux. We discuss a polarisation flare of the fading jet, scattering in an outflow, and synchrotron emission at the disc-magnetosphere boundary as possible origins, tentatively favouring the last.

papers.title: Lightest and heaviest nuclei as keys to the origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays
papers.abstract: The origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) has been a long-standing mystery. A unique feature of UHECRs originating in binary neutron star mergers (BNSMs) is two distinct populations of light elements -- those directly accelerated in the jets, and photo-disintegration products of massive nuclei accelerated in the bulk outflow. We show that Pierre Auger Observatory spectrum and composition data confirm the existence of the predicted two populations at $\geq \!7.2σ$ significance, having rigidity ($R\equiv E/Ze$) cutoffs agreeing with prior estimates. The data also favor 5-10% of UHECRs originating as r-process nuclei, a signature of a BNSM origin. Our results provide strong evidence that UHECRs are produced by merging neutron stars, and show how UHECRs and UHE-neutrinos elucidate otherwise inaccessible aspects of neutron star mergers.

papers.title: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
papers.abstract: Intranight optical variability (INOV) of blazars whose emission arises predominantly from a relativistic jet, has been widely linked to a combination of two key observational diagnostics: the fractional optical polarization ($P_{opt}$) and the Doppler boost arising from relativistic beaming of the jet's emission. To discern which of these two factors plays the dominant role, we investigate INOV of a well-defined representative sample of 8 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs, which are `low-synchrotron-peaked' blazars) whose jets exhibit a low degree of polarization ($P_{opt}$ < 3$\%$) but a large superluminal motion with c$β_{app}$ = 5c $-$ 31c (median = 10c). We report sensitive optical monitoring of these 8 `low-polarization superluminal quasars' (LPSQs) using a 1.3-metre telescope, in 20 sessions of minimum 3-hour duration. These data were supplemented with similarly high-quality monitoring data/results available in the literature for this sample, thus adding another 19 sessions. Duty cycle (DC) of strong INOV (amplitude $ψ> 5\%$) is found to be zero, applying the normally used $F_η$ test, and $\sim 7\%$ using the more powerful `enhanced $F$-test'. The small DC, despite the strong Doppler boost expected from the observed high superluminality, shows that strong INOV is much rarer among LPSQs, compared to high-polarization quasars, for which DC $(ψ> 5\%$) is found to be around 30%, even using the $F_η$ test. This provides the first compelling evidence that optical polarization is the primary diagnostic of INOV, while relativistic beaming plays a supportive role. Possible implications for the proposed mechanisms for INOV are pointed out.

papers.title: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
papers.abstract: In high-energy neutrino astrophysics, the identification of high-energy neutrino sources is a central goal, and jet-quiet active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have emerged as promising candidates. For this purpose, we present a theory-guided, intrinsic X-ray selected sample of hidden neutrino AGN candidates consisting of $28$ X-ray bright AGNs (X-HiNAC), combining the {\em Swift}/BAT and BASS surveys with dedicated {\em NuSTAR} observations and spectral analyses. We compile their intrinsic X-ray fluxes, spectral properties, luminosity distances, and supermassive black hole masses, to provide a coherent sample for neutrino source searches. The sample is physically motivated but remains model independent given that the neutrino flux is proportional to the intrinsic X-ray flux. Using the magnetically powered corona model, we also demonstrate the prospects for individual-source and stacking searches with IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT. We identify promising individual targets and find that stacking the remaining sources, excluding NGC 1068, could yield a $5σ$ detection within $\sim 5-15$ years under favorable model assumptions at the current and upcoming neutrino observatories. We highlight systematic uncertainties in the adopted source parameters, particularly the black hole masses, for which different measurement techniques can yield estimates differing by up to an order of magnitude. Such uncertainties can significantly affect the predicted neutrino emission, motivating more precise black hole mass measurements and improved broadband X-ray observations. Our findings motivate improved multiwavelength characterization of nearby AGNs and provide a guide for investigating their role as high-energy neutrino sources.

papers.title: Nova V1674 Her as a fast magnetic rotator
papers.abstract: We report on the results of our XMM-Newton and NuSTAR campaign targeting V1674 Her in October 2023. These observations were timed to investigate the post-nova quiescent state 28 months after the 2021 outburst, although the optical luminosity was still slowly declining. The X-ray spectra are well-modeled by a multi-temperature thermal plasma. While in the best fit temperature we find that the highest plasma temperature is indicative of a massive white dwarf ($M_{\text{WD}} \approx 1.35 M_\odot$), we caution that there is a degeneracy between the plasma temperature and the metallicity in the spectral fit, hindering a definitive constraint. Alternatively, the continuum can be phenomenologically described by a Comptonized component, although this model neglects the thermal bremsstrahlung component. Timing analysis reveals a stable 501.31 $\pm$ 0.19 s modulation in the post-quiescent phase, whose amplitude diminishes with increasing energy; this is quite typical in intermediate polars (IP). The phase alignment between the quiescent and early post-outburst Chandra spin-folded light curves suggests that the soft X-ray emission originates from the same polar regions, which quickly re-established accretion following the eruption. V1674 Her belongs to a growing class of novae that are also IPs, and is one of four in which the modulation with rotation was observed during the outburst supersoft X-ray phase. We propose that the fast rise in outburst was due to a fast or centrifugal magnetic rotator wind, causing rapid mass loss instead of the commonly assumed radiation pressure wind.

papers.title: Formation of Micron-sized Presolar Graphite Grains in Low-energy Supernova Ejecta
papers.abstract: Presolar graphite grains with supernova isotopic signatures provide direct evidence that large graphite grains formed in supernova ejecta. However, theoretical calculations of dust formation in supernovae have typically predicted graphite grains smaller than $0.1\,{\rm μm}$, leaving unclear the physical conditions required to form those grains with radii of order $1\,{\rm μm}$. We systematically investigate graphite nucleation and growth in expanding supernova ejecta by varying the explosion energy, ejecta mass, initial ejecta radius, and ejected $^{56}$Ni mass. We use a simplified one-zone model that follows the temperature and density evolution including adiabatic cooling, radiative cooling, and heating by radioactive nickel. We show that the final graphite grain size is mainly determined by the product of the mass density of atomic carbon available for grain growth and the local cooling timescale, both evaluated at a reference temperature of $2000\,{\rm K}$. Our models show that graphite growth is favored by lower explosion energy, larger ejecta mass, and smaller initial ejecta radius, which keep the gas denser near the graphite-condensation temperature. When radioactive heating and radiative cooling are included, explosions with $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{50}\,{\rm erg}$ and $M_{\rm Ni}\lesssim10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ can form $1$-$10\,μ{\rm m}$ graphite grains in the ejected helium layer or carbon-oxygen core, whereas $E_{\rm exp}\sim10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ models do not. These results suggest that micron-sized presolar supernova graphite preferentially forms in faint-supernova-like explosions with low explosion energies, little ejected nickel, and helium layer or carbon-oxygen core ejecta.

papers.title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
papers.abstract: We report updated mass and radius measurements for the millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 obtained with pulse profile modeling of the emission from the far-ultraviolet to the hard X-rays. Using an extended 2.56 Ms Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR (NICER) dataset together with XMM-Newton, Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope ARray and Hubble Space Telescope observations, we perform Bayesian inference with models describing the thermal emission from hot spots of increasing complexities, together with the rest of the warm NS surface, as well as the non-thermal emission component represented by a phase-dependent (pulsed) power-law. With this comprehensive model and broadband data set, as well as radio timing priors on the mass, distance and inclination, our headline result for PSR J0437-4715 led to a mass M = 1.377(-0.034)(+0.038) Msun and an equatorial radius Req = 11.35(-0.39)(+0.40) km, one of the narrowest measurements of Req from NICER observations of millisecond pulsars. The geometric configuration favors a non-antipodal hot spot distribution, as noted in previous analyses of this pulsar. When combined with recent measurements of M and Req of other pulsars, the tight constraints from PSR J0437-4715 further reduce the allowed range of the dense matter equation of state, excluding those that predict radii above 12.0 km (at the 68% level) for all NS masses.

papers.title: First Light with the Dark100 Array of PANOSETI Telescopes at Palomar Observatory
papers.abstract: Dark100 is the first phase of an extensive array of Panoramic SETI (PANOSETI) telescopes at Palomar Observatory, California. PANOSETI telescopes are small, 0.5-m Fresnel lens telescopes instrumented with 1024-pixel silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) cameras. The telescopes were originally designed to search for ultra-fast optical transients, but they also function as cost-effective imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). Dark100 will use seven of these widely separated IACTs to map the ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma-ray sources on the Galactic Plane at high resolution. Dark100 will also leverage the IACT technique to search for evidence of ultra-heavy dark matter in a mass range that extends beyond 100 TeV. Deployment of the first four telescopes and enclosures was completed in December 2025, and commissioning of the next three is scheduled to finish by the end of 2026. The array has so far collected more than 100 hours of 3-telescope data on sources including the Crab Nebula and Markarian 421. Here we present the current status of Dark100.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Emission from LS 5039: A 30-500 GeV Excess and Phase-Resolved Broadband Spectral Modeling
papers.abstract: LS~5039 is a well-studied $γ$-ray binary exhibiting strong orbital modulation from GeV to TeV energies. We present a phase-resolved analysis of 17.3~yr of \textit{Fermi}-LAT observations and identify an additional $γ$-ray excess in the $\sim30$--$500$~GeV at a significance of $\sim7.9σ$. The phase-resolved spectra show pronounced orbital dependence above $\sim10$~GeV, with the inferior-conjunction more complex than the superior-conjunction. To investigate the broadband spectral energy distribution, we combine the \textit{Fermi}-LAT spectra with published H.E.S.S.\ and HAWC measurements and compare purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models using the Bayesian information criterion. In both intervals, relativistic-Maxwellian and magnetospheric components dominate below $\sim10$~GeV, while shock-accelerated electrons account for much of the GeV--TeV continuum. The purely leptonic fits leave residuals at $30$--$500$~GeV and underpredict the HAWC measurements above $\sim100$~TeV. In the local one-zone intrabinary shock apex model, synchrotron cooling and Klein-Nishina suppression make the ultra-high-energy emission difficult to reproduce, although more complex leptonic scenarios remain possible. Adding a phenomenological proton component improves the broadband description, with stronger relative support during superior-conjunction than inferior-conjunction. However, the proton parameters remain weakly constrained and the fast-escape hadronic interpretation is energetically challenging, so a hadronic origin is not uniquely established. Future high-sensitivity, phase-resolved observations at multi-TeV and ultra-high energies will be required to test this interpretation.

papers.title: Long-term variability of the 35-day cycle in Her X-1
papers.abstract: Her X-1 is an eclipsing X-ray binary system consisting of an accreting neutron star and an optical component HZ Her. In addition to the 1.24-s X-ray pulsations and the 1.7-d orbital period, the system also shows a 35-day X-ray variability related to the precessional motion of a tilted and twisted accretion disk around the neutron star. The long-term persistence of the 35-day X-ray variability suggests the presence of a stable clock mechanism, most likely free precession of the magnetized neutron star. We have studied the long-term behavior of the 35-day cycle of Her X-1 using all available CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI data and archival turn-on moments of the 35-day cycle spanning more than 50 years. We have used a sliding-window averaged X-ray phase light curve and the classical O-C (observed minus calculated) diagram for individual 35-day turn-ons to inspect the long-term trends of the O-C diagram. The O-C diagram demonstrates two similar parabolic trends separated by an anomalous low state (ALS) of the source suggesting a secular decrease in the 35-d precession period with $\dot P_\text{35} =(-1.3\pm0.2)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ and $\dot P_\text{35} =(-4.7\pm0.1)\times10^{-5} \,\mathrm{~s\,s}^{-1}$ before and after the ALS, respectively. We conclude that the decay of the 35-day period as inferred from the O-C analysis can be interpreted in terms of the direct relationship between the change of the precessional period of the accretion disk to the long-term decrease of the period of the free precessional neutron star - due to continued accumulation of accreted matter.

papers.title: SN 2025dys: A luminous supernova explosion from a partially stripped helium star
papers.abstract: We present well-sampled multi-band imaging and low- to medium-resolution spectroscopic observations of the early-discovered Type~II supernova (SN)~2025dys. The photometric evolution exhibits a rise time of $\sim$\,18 days ($r$ band) and a rapid decline transitioning to the radioactive decay tail at $\sim$\,70 days. SN~2025dys is among the high-luminosity events with a peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of $L_{\rm opt}=8.57\times10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Early X-ray emission was identified, displaying a luminosity of $7.55\times10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The observational investigation points to a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar medium with a mass of $M_{\rm CSM}\approx0.5$--$0.7\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, suggesting a partially stripped, hydrogen-poor inner ejecta with a relatively low mass of $M_{\rm ej}\approx2.5\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The explosion possessed a kinetic energy of $E_{\rm k}\approx0.3\text{--}0.5$~foe and yielded a synthesized nickel mass of $M_{\rm Ni}\approx0.042_{-0.011}^{+0.012}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. These physical parameters indicate an extreme mass-loss episode before the explosion, characterized by a high mass-loss rate of $\dot{M} \gtrsim 0.01\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$. SN~2025dys represents a stripped progenitor, intrinsically resembling a Type~IIb or even a Type~Ib SN, that exploded within a dense, hydrogen-rich circumstellar environment.

papers.title: Disk-Corona Energy Balance Evolves with Flux State in the Quasar PDS 456
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-term X-ray spectral evolution of the highly luminous, radio-quiet quasar PDS 456 using AstroSat observations obtained in 2019 and 2021 together with archival XMM-Newton, NuSTAR and Suzaku observations spanning 2001-2024. The AstroSat observations provide valuable coverage following the bright flaring state observed in 2018, revealing that the source underwent a relatively quiescent phase in 2019 before re-brightening in 2021. During the AstroSat epochs, PDS 456 exhibits a harder-when-brighter spectral trend, whereas the long-term XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, and Suzaku observations confirm the overall softer-when-fainter behavior. This behavior is consistent with the presence of a very cool corona (~15 keV), possibly driven by a strong incident photon field for upscattering, as suggested by a prominent big blue bump. Broadband spectral modeling of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations, complemented by the 2021 AstroSat flaring epoch and interpreted within the self-consistent physical framework reXcor, indicates that the disk-corona energy balance evolves with flux. In low-flux states, the spectrum is reflection-dominated, implying efficient illumination of the inner accretion disk by a compact corona. In contrast, high-flux states show an enhanced contribution from the warm Comptonizing region at larger coronal heights. The Fe Kα emission line displays a positive correlation with the 2-10 keV continuum flux at low to intermediate flux levels, while deviations at the highest flux states suggest a reduced relative reflection contribution as the warm corona becomes energetically dominant.

papers.title: As a matter of reconstruction -- varying the magnetic Prandtl number in implicit large eddy simulations
papers.abstract: The magnetic Prandtl number ($\mathrm{Pm}$), the ratio of viscosity to magnetic diffusivity, spans many orders of magnitude in astrophysical plasmas. It shapes how turbulence amplifies and structures magnetic fields. In direct numerical simulations (DNS) the viscosity and magnetic diffusivity can be controlled explicitly and independently, whereas in implicit large eddy simulations (ILES) they are set by the numerical scheme. We test whether, in a finite-volume code, $\mathrm{Pm}$ can be varied through the reconstruction scheme by applying different methods to the hydro and magnetic variables. As a proof of concept, we simulate driven, subsonic, homogeneous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence using five pairs of hydrodynamic and magnetic reconstruction schemes at varying resolutions. We measure the effective viscosity and resistivity from the energy transfer between scales. Reconstructing the magnetic field at higher order than the fluid raises the effective magnetic Prandtl number and vice versa. We demonstrate that a mix of second- and third-order reconstruction alone results in a $\gtrsim20\times$ change in $\mathrm{Pm}$. A comparison of DNS with matched explicit dissipation at these values agrees with the ILES. Mixed reconstruction thus offers a simple and efficient way to explore $\mathrm{Pm} \not\simeq 1$ in ILES without adding explicit dissipation.

papers.title: Wide-field search for submicrosecond optical and gamma transients as manifestation of primordial black holes evaporation with the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array
papers.abstract: We demonstrated in our papers [Panov, 2021; Panov,2025), that the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array physics, originally designed for research in cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, can also be used for wide-field searches for very rare submicrosecond optical transients of astrophysical origin. The papers \cite{PANOV-2021,PANOV-2025} presented the results of the first four seasons of optical transient searches (2018--2022) and the resulting upper limits on the flux of corresponding events. The present paper presents data processing from two new seasons of optical transient searches (2022--2024). This paper further develops a method for searching for narrow spatiotemporal groups of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays (above 100\,TeV). Since the evaporation of relic black holes can be accompanied by both by the emission of a short light pulse and by a flash of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays, a multimessenger technique for searching for black hole evaporation was in fact implemented in this work, where two different methods are implemented within a single instrument. The search for narrow spatiotemporal groups of gamma-rays was carried out in time windows of 1000\,$μ$s, 100\,$μ$s, and 6\,$μ$s. Since narrow groups of gamma were not detected, the upper limit on their frequency were obtained as $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$. The upper limit on the number of submicrosecond optical transients have also been updated: $10^{-4}\mathrm{erg/s/cm}^2$ as $5\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$.

papers.title: Enhanced Detectability of Very-High-Energy Gamma Rays from Off-Axis Short Gamma-Ray Bursts: Impacts of Structured Jets and External Inverse-Compton Scattering
papers.abstract: The binary neutron star merger GW170817 established a direct link between gravitational waves and short gamma-ray bursts (sGRBs), whose afterglows are commonly interpreted as nonthermal emission from structured relativistic jets viewed off-axis. Some sGRBs exhibit extended or plateau X-ray emission, suggesting prolonged central-engine activity. These X-ray photons can serve as seed photons for external inverse-Compton (EIC) scattering by relativistic electrons in the jet, producing very-high-energy (VHE) gamma rays. However, how the angular structure of the jet affects the detectability of EIC emission remains insufficiently explored. Here, we investigate EIC emission from off-axis structured jets and assess its detectability with the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). We find that EIC emission powered by extended and/or plateau X-rays produces detectable VHE signals from nearby sGRBs, particularly during the early afterglow, significantly outshining synchrotron self-Compton emission. In our adopted models, Gaussian and power-law jets produce brighter off-axis EIC emission than a top-hat jet, extending the viewing-angle range over which VHE emission may be detectable. These results demonstrate that early VHE observations with CTAO can probe both prolonged central-engine activity and the angular structure of relativistic jets in sGRBs.

papers.title: Effect of quark-hadron phase transitions on the neutron star mass distribution
papers.abstract: The neutron star (NS) mass distribution serves as a crucial probe of the dense matter equation of state (EOS) and core-collapse supernova explosion mechanisms. Although observations reveal a bimodal NS mass distribution, existing theoretical simulations often struggle to naturally reproduce the high-mass peak, and the impact of the quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in high-density nuclear matter remains largely unexplored. Employing the 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamics code GR1D with hybrid EOSs incorporating a first-order PT (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2), we systematically simulate core-collapse supernovae for progenitors with zero-age main-sequence masses ranging from 13 to 120 $M_\odot$. Our results reveal a threefold impact of the PT onset density on the final supernova fate: in low-compactness progenitors, an early PT truncates accretion and produces less massive NSs; in the critical-compactness regime, it facilitates successful explosions; and in high-compactness progenitors, it accelerates black hole formation. Compared with the $\sim 1.4\,M_\odot$ peak typical of the conventional core-collapse scenario, the inclusion of the PT produces NSs with masses centered around $1.70\,M_\odot$ for RDF1.1 and within $1.55$--$1.70\,M_\odot$ for RDF1.2. Furthermore, we identify a novel formation channel whereby low-compactness progenitors with failed initial shocks can form more massive NSs via a PT-induced second shock. Due to the fixed nature of the PT boundary, the final NS masses exhibit a pronounced clustering effect. This study elucidates the critical role of the quark-hadron PT in shaping the NS mass distribution, providing important astrophysical constraints on the properties of high-density nuclear matter and the formation mechanism of massive NSs.

papers.title: More Eccentric, Not Always Less Detectable: High Mass Holds Its Ground, Low Mass Loses Reach
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from eccentric compact binary coalescences trace dynamical binary formation, but matched-filtering searches responsible for most detections rely on quasicircular templates. Quantifying any sensitivity loss is crucial for assessing population completeness and the need for dedicated eccentric template banks. We present the first systematic GstLAL search study spanning eccentricities up to $e_{\rm 15Hz}=0.99$ and broad ranges of chirp mass, mass ratio, inclination, and aligned spin. Using TEOBResumS-Dalí waveforms, we inject eccentric signals and measure recovered signal-to-noise ratio, signal-consistency statistics, false-alarm rate, and sensitive volume and distance. For high-mass binaries ($\mathcal{M}_c\gtrsim30\,M_\odot$), sensitive distance is nearly independent of eccentricity, demonstrating that greater eccentricity does not necessarily reduce search sensitivity. In contrast, for low-mass binaries, sensitive distance falls by up to $\sim50\%$ near $e_{\rm 15Hz}\approx0.75$. Although the absolute loss in reach is modest given their low quasicircular sensitivity, this relative reduction exceeds the increase in sensitive distance between the second and third observing runs of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA collaboration and is consistent with previous low-mass studies. We also find that waveform matches at fixed source parameters substantially overpredict search sensitivity loss, meaning that the pipeline's signal-consistency test and maximization over its template bank mitigate much of the predicted sensitivity loss. This highlights the need for end-to-end injection campaigns to establish the detectability of eccentric binaries.

papers.title: HAWC, Fermi-LAT and Chandra Detections of High Energy Particles in the S106 Star Forming Region
papers.abstract: Local star-forming regions have recently been the subject of scrutiny as cosmic-ray accelerators and sources of ultra-high-energy gamma-ray emissions. The Cygnus-X region is one of the richest star forming regions in the galaxy and over the last few decades has been extensively studied. Here we report the detection of a star-forming region located in the southern part of Cygnus-X, Sharpless 106 (S106), using the HAWC Observatory. The S106 region is spatially located near the cataloged gamma-ray source 1LHAASO J2027+3657. In this work, we perform a multi-wavelength analysis of S106, by combining HAWC data with re-analysis of Fermi-LAT and archival Chandra data. We construct a fully leptonic model for the multi-wavelength emission from S106 from a single population of high-energy leptons, with the gamma-rays greater than 1 TeV being produced by inverse Compton scattering of the locally-produced IR photon field from S106 itself. Our models show that hadronic mechanisms are not always required to explain the observed flux from gamma-ray star-forming regions and that understanding the specific details of local photon fields is crucial to modeling the multi-wavelength emission from star-forming regions.

papers.title: MAGIKS: Multimodal Alignment and Gravitational-Wave-Conditioned Interaction for Kilonova Search
papers.abstract: We present MAGIKS, a multimodal framework for gravitational-wave (GW)-triggered kilonova identification that formulates counterpart search as query-conditioned gallery retrieval.
